US8069128B2.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier.

Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering.entity_name: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach
Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages and present potentially misclassified messages to the user.

Classification Model.description: A model generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, maintained within memory on a user's client device as memory resident only, and not stored on disk or in another persistent data store.

First Message Filter.description: A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into various folders for a user and is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.

Second Multi-Pass Message Filter.description: A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis and to perform a second pass on sorted messages to generate a misclassification identification of sorted messages.

Network Device.description: A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform actions for managing delivery of a message over a network.

Transceiver.description: A component of the network device used to send and receive data over a network.

Processor.description: A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.

Message.description: An email or similar item delivered over a network that is sorted into message folders and analyzed by message filters.

Message Folders.description: A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by a message filter and to which misclassified messages can be moved.

Non-Persistent Memory Location.description: A memory location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, from which the model is purged and not stored on disk or another persistent data store.

Persistent Store.description: A data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

Client Device.description: A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.

Processor Readable Storage Medium.description: A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

Naive Bayes Classifier.description: A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.

Misclassification Identification.description: An identification of sorted messages generated by the second pass, displayed so that at least one misclassified message can be moved to a different message folder.

First Pass Analysis.description: An analysis performed on a plurality of messages previously sorted into folders, used to train the multi-pass message filter and generate a classification model.

Second Pass.description: A pass using the generated classification model on the sorted messages to score each message and identify misclassified messages.

Sender Information.description: Information within messages read during the first pass, including sender address and whether the sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.

Message Headers.description: Information within messages read during the first pass, including a subject and an originating network address.

Message Contents.description: The content of messages read during the first pass analysis.

Attachments.description: Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

Address Book.description: An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis of whether a message sender's address is present.

User.description: A person for whom messages are sorted into folders and who is presented a list of potentially misclassified messages and enabled to move identified messages to another folder.

Interface.description: An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.

endpoints: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach

Multi-Pass Message Filter.description: A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.

First Message Filter.description: A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.

Client Device.description: A device that executes the multi-pass message filter, generates and stores second classification data in a non-persistent memory store, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and displays information enabling a user to move messages to another folder.

Network Device.description: A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network to the message folders.

Message Folder.description: A folder into which messages are sorted; messages may be identified as stored in an incorrect message folder and moved to another message folder.

First Classification Data.description: Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter when assigning messages to message folders.

Persistent Store.description: A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.

Message.description: A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as sorted into an incorrect message folder.

Address Book.description: A book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in the address book may be analyzed to generate second classification data.

Network.description: A communications network over which messages are communicated to the message folders.
